subject: RFI: Log preservation, legal-hold exports & forensic snapshotting
messages:
From: Diane Hollis <diane.hollis@acme-corp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: RFI: Log preservation and exportability requirements

Vivek,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is Acme's RFI worksheet for logs — we need written answers to the capability questions below to support our procurement and legal team. High-level asks:

1) Retention tiers and configurable retention windows for (a) API request/response logs, (b) audit trail (admin actions), (c) KV cache/prefix metadata.
2) Export formats supported (schema + timestamp fidelity) and whether we can get a delta export vs. full bucket export.
3) Forensic snapshotting: how we produce tamper-evident bundles for legal holds and incident response.
4) Chain-of-custody / attestations you can provide for exported artifacts.
5) Typical turnaround SLA for ad-hoc exports (48/72/120 hrs) and the transport options you support.

Please answer inline in the worksheet and provide any SOPs or technical specs. We would like a sample delta export (small window) if possible so our engineering team can validate ingestion.

Attachment: Acme-RFI-logs.xlsx (questionnaire)

Regards,
Diane Hollis
Senior Security Program Manager
Acme Corp

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Hollis <diane.hollis@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 19:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFI: Log preservation and exportability requirements

Diane — thanks for the worksheet. Answering at a high level here and attaching a concise technical spec and SOP; we can follow up with a short call to walk the team through the sample extract.

Summary answers (details in attached redwood-log-export-spec_v1.pdf and sop-log-harvest.md):

1) Retention tiers
- Hosted API request/response logs: configurable per-tenant: 30 days (default), 90d, 365d, 730d. Policy can be set at service-level; archived snapshots available beyond 730d via reserved capacity retention add-on.
- Admin/audit trail (configuration changes, role updates): immutable audit ledger kept 365d by default, configurable to 730d for enterprise plans; legal-hold preserves immutable snapshot beyond configured retention.
- KV cache/prefix metadata: ephemeral by default (kept in-memory for active sessions). For customers that opt into long-term KV preservation (rare), we surface explicit export APIs; retention depends on configuration and contractual terms.

2) Export formats & fidelity
- Supported formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) with strict schema, Parquet (columnar) for bulk analytics, and gzipped tarballs for bundles.
- Timestamps: All events include both event_timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC) and ingestion_monotonic_id (64-bit hex monotonic sequence) to preserve ordering.
- Delta exports: Supported. You can request an incremental export by event_timestamp range or monotonic_id range. We include range markers and checkpoint tokens to enable resumed transfer.

3) Forensic snapshotting
- We produce tamper-evident bundles by signing a manifest (SHA256 checksums) and attaching signed assertions (timestamped by our HSM-backed KMS). Bundles are accompanied by a signed hash chain and an export manifest that includes cryptographic proofs.
- We can produce a full-system snapshot or scoped snapshots (tenant, route, or specific API keys).

4) Chain-of-custody / attestations
- We provide a certificate-style attestation for each export that records who requested it, what was exported (manifest), time window, and the SHA256 checksum signed by our service key.
- For high-assurance requests we can coordinate a notarized handoff via an approved third-party (e.g., secure courier or eDiscovery vendor) and provide a signed handoff log.

5) SLA & transport options
- Typical turnaround for standard exports: 72 hours. For expedited (business-critical/legal hold) we offer 24–48 hr SLA on enterprise support plans.
- Transport: S3 presigned multipart upload URL (preferred), SCP/SFTP over customer gateway, or dedicated VPN tunnel for large transfers. For very large bundles we can ship encrypted storage appliances under contract.

Next steps:
- We will produce a 1GB sample delta export for the time window you specify — delivery via S3 presigned link.
- Attached: redwood-log-export-spec_v1.pdf (detailed schema + sample payload), sop-log-harvest.md (internal runbook with steps we follow), evidence_bundle_manifest_template.csv (manifest template).

Let me know a 30-minute slot tomorrow for a quick walkthrough.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-log-export-spec_v1.pdf (pdf), sop-log-harvest.md (text), evidence_bundle_manifest_template.csv (csv)]

- For SLA: if we place a legal hold during off-hours, is the 24–48 hr expedited SLA measured from the time of request or from next business day?

Also — please send the sample delta export for the window 2027-03-01T00:00:00Z — 2027-03-01T02:00:00Z. Small subset will do.

Thanks,
Diane

Subject: Re: RFI: Log preservation and exportability requirements

Diane — good questions, here are the clarifications and concrete next steps.

1) Monotonic ID semantics
- monotonic_id is a strictly-increasing 64-bit sequence assigned at ingestion boundary per shard. Exports include shard_id and checkpoint_token which encodes the last_monotonic_id exported. The sample delta will include a small reordering example (we demote events received out-of-order into the stream but monotonic_id preserves arrival order). We'll include a mapping table in the sample manifest to show how checkpoint tokens resume from a given monotonic_id.

2) Attestations / notarization
- Our signed attestations (HSM-signed manifest + timestamp) meet industry standard evidentiary requirements for digital preservation and are accepted by several of our enterprise/legal customers. If your counsel requires physical notarization, we can support on a case-by-case basis (third-party eDiscovery vendor or notarized courier). For most cases the digital attestation is sufficient.

3) SLA measurement
- Expedited SLA is measured from the time the export request is received by our support intake system (24/7). If you submit the request during off-hours it still counts from receipt; however, manifesting and packaging may be performed in the next operational window depending on team availability — we will state exact ETA in the intake ticket.

Delivery plan for requested sample window (2027-03-01T00:00:00Z — 2027-03-01T02:00:00Z):
- We will deliver a ~25MB NDJSON delta containing event_timestamp/monotonic_id, plus a signed manifest and a small readme that shows how to resume from checkpoint_token. Delivery via S3 presigned URL. ETA: 2027-03-16T12:00:00Z.

Security notes: bundle will be encrypted in-transit and at rest (AES-256); manifest signed with KMS-backed key.

If acceptable, we'll open a HubSpot ticket and generate the presigned link for secure download. Otherwise we can arrange an SFTP drop.

Next steps: I'll have Marissa open the ticket and Ben coordinate the sample export; expect the sample link tomorrow.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
